sections.h2: Where is Newington, Connecticut, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Newington is a mostly residential suburb in Hartford County, about 8 miles south of downtown Hartford. It belongs to the Capitol Planning Region, and the 2020 census counted 30,536 residents.

The town is compact, at 13.1 square miles with almost no water, so its density is about 2,326 people per square mile. It is bordered by Hartford on the north and, going clockwise, by Wethersfield, Rocky Hill, Berlin, New Britain, Farmington and West Hartford.

Most of Newington is neighborhoods of houses, with one major commercial spine, the Berlin Turnpike, running through it. If you own a house here, your buyers are mostly other Greater Hartford residents.

sections.h2: How did Newington become its own town?
sections.html:
Settlers from Wethersfield first took up land on its western edge in 1636, and the area was known as West Farms. In 1721 the colonial General Assembly gave the name Newington, meaning the new town in the meadow, but the town did not incorporate until July 10, 1871, after Wethersfield declined to pay for better roads to the railroads.

Growth came in waves. A trolley started in 1894 and linked Hartford and New Britain, and the town grew from 5,449 people in 1940 to 9,110 in 1950, a jump that tied for the fastest in the state with North Haven. By 1960 it had 17,664.

That postwar boom built much of the housing you see now. Houses from that era are now several decades old, so older mechanical systems are a common part of a resale.

sections.h2: What is the Berlin Turnpike, and how does it affect nearby houses?
sections.html:
The Berlin Turnpike is Newington's main commercial road. It began as the Hartford and New Haven Turnpike, authorized in 1798, and it was renamed the Berlin Turnpike in 1942 when it was widened from 18 feet to 200 feet.

Over time, small businesses along the corridor have given way to larger chain stores. Stew Leonard's, Walmart and Target appear on the town's list of top employers.

  • Houses near the turnpike are close to shopping and highway access.
  • Houses on interior streets, such as along Main Street or Willard Avenue, are in quieter residential areas.
  • Newington Junction has three historic districts and the Newington Junction Railroad Depot, built in 1870 and on the National Register.

Your location relative to these areas is a reasonable thing to mention to any buyer.

The town's own financial report for fiscal year 2024 lists Hartford Hospital's Newington campus as the largest employer, with 1,481 employees. The Connecticut Department of Transportation also has its headquarters here, at 2800 Berlin Turnpike.

sections.h2: What does the closing of old factories mean for Newington?
sections.html:
Manufacturing used to be a larger part of Newington's economy. The Torrington Company, which made automobile parts and surgical staplers, and the adhesives maker Loctite both left in the mid-1990s, and the defense industry shrank.

Shopping centers, condominium development and continued activity on the Berlin Turnpike helped the town avoid a sharper decline. For a seller, the takeaway is that the economy today leans on healthcare, state government and retail, and employers such as the hospital and the state transportation department are right in town.

sections.h2: What landmarks and parks make Newington recognizable?
sections.html:
Newington is best known for Mill Pond Falls, a 16-foot natural waterfall in central town that appears on the town seal and is described as the smallest natural waterfall in the country. Mill Pond Park is open year-round, with a walking path that crosses the falls on a footbridge.

The town holds a Waterfall Festival every September in the town center. Other local landmarks include the Willard Homestead from 1730, the General Martin Kellogg House from 1808, the National Iwo Jima Memorial on Ella Grasso Boulevard, and the Lucy Robbins Welles Library, which opened in 1939. Parks and a library close by are the sort of details a buyer will want to hear about.

sections.h2: How do residents get around Newington?
sections.html:
Newington has one of the state's more distinctive transit connections. CTfastrak, Connecticut's first bus rapid transit corridor, opened on March 28, 2015, with a stop at Newington Junction on a separated busway between Hartford and New Britain.

  • Connecticut Transit routes 41, 45, 47 and 69 serve the town.
  • The 907 Newington Express runs express service to downtown Hartford.
  • The town center is about 8 miles from Hartford's Union Station.

Buyers who work in Hartford or New Britain often ask about this busway, so mention it if your house is near Newington Junction.

sections.h2: How do Newington schools and town services work?
sections.html:
Newington Public Schools has seven public schools. The four elementary schools, Elizabeth Green, Anna Reynolds, John Paterson and Ruth Chaffee, teach kindergarten through grade 4, and children attend the school for their district.

Martin Kellogg and John Wallace middle schools teach grades 5 through 8, and Newington High School serves grades 9 through 12. The town hall and police department are in the renovated former 1950s high school.

Fire protection comes from an all-volunteer department founded in 1917 and run by an elected board of three fire commissioners. A volunteer ambulance service provides basic life support, with advanced support from American Medical Response at other times.

sections.h2: How is Newington governed, and where do you go for permits?
sections.html:
Newington has a council-manager government under a charter received in 1871. A nine-member Town Council serves two-year terms, and an elected mayor presides over it and votes. The council meets on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month.

Ask the Revenue Collector's office for the figures on your own account before closing.

sections.h2: What conveyance tax does a Newington seller pay?
sections.html:
Connecticut puts a conveyance tax on each deed. The base rates are three-quarters of one percent for the state and one-quarter of one percent for the town, so a $300,000 house produces $3,000 at those rates.

  • Over $800,000, a higher state rate applies to the excess.
  • The seller's attorney or agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded.
  • The state lists exemptions, including transfers between spouses and a deed in lieu of foreclosure for a principal residence.

Ask the Newington Town Clerk whether any additional municipal rate applies.

sections.h2: How can you sell a Newington house?
sections.html:
Newington owners generally choose between a traditional listing and a direct cash sale.

  • A listing can reach a broad group of buyers but includes showings, inspections and financing contingencies.
  • A cash sale usually closes faster and has no financing contingency.
  • Cash Home Buyers buys houses in Newington as they are, including those with deferred repairs.

Send us your address and condition details, and we will respond with an offer you can weigh against listing it.

faqs.a: Newington is in Hartford County, about 8 miles south of Hartford. It borders Hartford, Wethersfield, Rocky Hill, Berlin, New Britain, Farmington and West Hartford.

faqs.q: What is the population of Newington?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 30,536 people in Newington.

faqs.q: Who are the largest employers in Newington?
faqs.a: Hartford Hospital's Newington campus is first with 1,481 employees, followed by the Town of Newington and the Connecticut Department of Transportation, per the town's 2024 financial report.

faqs.q: Is there public transit in Newington?
faqs.a: Yes. CTfastrak has a Newington Junction station, and Connecticut Transit routes 41, 45, 47 and 69 plus the 907 Newington Express serve the town.

faqs.q: How much conveyance tax do I owe selling in Newington?
faqs.a: At base rates, one percent of the sale price for a residential house: three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town. A higher state rate applies above $800,000.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newington house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses as-is, so you do not need to repair or clean before selling.
